request.prompt: The Tidewatch: a squat stone watchtower standing on a black rock headland above a night sea, seen from off the water at a low angle. The tower is four storeys of weathered grey blockwork with a shallow conical roof and one large square lamp window near the top facing the sea — and the lamp window is DARK, no light in it, which is the whole point of the picture. Below and in front of the tower a tide-cut stair of wet black rock drops in broken flights to a small shingle landing at the waterline, with a cave mouth in the rock beside it. Low swell, foam on the rocks, a bank of cloud with a little moonlight behind it. No figures, no boats, no text.
request.style_note: The Tidewatch, in the same hand throughout: cold night palette of wet black rock, grey weathered stone and a green-black sea, painted concept art with visible brushwork, moonlight as the only warm value, no saturated colour anywhere. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset or a caption.
